14 An object hangs by means of two cords around two rods, as shown.

The object is held in equilibrium by the forces F1 and F2. The object weighs 10 N. There is
negligible friction between the rods and cords. Angle θ is 90°.
Which row of the table gives an angle θ of 90°?
F1 / N
F2 / N
A

hints: Notice the rods act like frictionless pulleys, so the tension in the left sloping cord equals $F_1$ and the tension in the right sloping cord equals $F_2$.
Because angle $\theta$ between the two tensions is $90^{\circ}$, their vector sum has magnitude $\sqrt{F_1^2+F_2^2}$ and this must balance the $10 \text{ N}$ weight.

Compare the two cord angles to the vertical in the diagram: the left cord is more horizontal, so its vertical component per newton is smaller and $F_1$ must be the smaller of the 6.0 N and 8.0 N pair.
walkthrough: The rods are frictionless, so tension is transmitted unchanged. The force pulling up-left on the knot equals $F_1$ and the force pulling up-right equals $F_2$.
At the knot three forces act in equilibrium: $F_1$ along the left cord, $F_2$ along the right cord with $90^{\circ}$ between them, and $10 \text{ N}$ vertically down from the object.
For equilibrium the vector sum of $F_1$ and $F_2$ must be $10 \text{ N}$ vertically up. Because they are perpendicular, Pythagoras gives $\sqrt{F_1^2+F_2^2}=10 \text{ N}$.
Test the numbers: $\sqrt{6.0^2+8.0^2}=\sqrt{36+64}=\sqrt{100}=10 \text{ N}$, while $\sqrt{4.0^2+6.0^2} \approx 7.2 \text{ N}$. Only the 6.0 N and 8.0 N pair works.

Choose the order from horizontal equilibrium. The left cord is more horizontal than the right cord, so $F_1 \sin\phi_1 = F_2 \sin\phi_2$ requires the larger angle $\phi_1$ to pair with the smaller tension. Hence $F_1=6.0 \text{ N}$ and $F_2=8.0 \text{ N}$. This is option C.

A.explanation: Resultant $\sqrt{4.0^2+6.0^2} \approx 7.2 \text{ N}$ is less than the $10 \text{ N}$ weight, so it cannot balance the object.

B.explanation: Resultant $\sqrt{6.0^2+4.0^2} \approx 7.2 \text{ N}$ is less than the $10 \text{ N}$ weight, so it cannot balance the object.

C.explanation: Resultant $\sqrt{6.0^2+8.0^2}=10 \text{ N}$ exactly balances the $10 \text{ N}$ weight, with the smaller $F_1$ on the more horizontal left cord.

D.explanation: Resultant magnitude is $10 \text{ N}$ but $F_1 > F_2$ is the wrong way round because the more horizontal left cord must provide the smaller tension for horizontal balance.
